lamentor

la:verb:lambo.html:
lambo, bi, bitum (
perf. lambuerunt, ), 3, v. a.
root lap-; Gr. λάπτω, λαφύσσω; Lat. labrum, labium; Germ. Löffel, spoon; Eng. lip
, to lick, lap; to touch (class.; cf.: lingo, sugo, ligurio).
Lit.: hi canes, quos tribunal meum vides lambere,: lagonae collum,: lambent cibos (pisces),: manum,: sanguinem,: crustula,: jucundasque puer qui lamberat ore placentas, Lucil. ap. : lambent sanguinem,to lick up, to lap,; cf. : te gurgite mersum unda feret, piscesque inpastivulnera lambent,.—
Transf., of a river, to flow by, to wash, bathe: vel quae loca fabulosus Lambit Hydaspes,washes,.—Of fire, to lick, to reach, play upon: flamma summum properabat lambere tectum,: innoxia mollis Lambere flamma comas (Iuli),: Aetna attollit globos flammarum et sidera lambit,.—Of the ivy: quorum imagines lambunt hederae sequaces,to encircle,: Tedia non lambit Cluviam,caress, fondle,: tribunal unius legati,to fawn upon, court,.—In mal. part., et saep.

la:noun:lampas.html:
lampăs, ădis (late Lat. also lampă-da, ae, :
lampadarum,), f., = λαμπάς, a light, torch, flambeau (mostly poet.; cf.: lucerna, lychnus, laterna).
Lit.: lampades ardentes,: illatae lampades, Att. ap. : lampadas igniferas,: vidi argenteum Cupidinem cum lampade,: pinguis,: pingues lampades,: ardens,: Salmoneus, dum flammas Jovis imitatur, lampada quassans,: lampadibus densum rapuit funale coruscis,with torches,; : lampas ignis,.—Used at weddings, a wedding-torch: tene hane lampadem,; . —Hence, poet.: lampade primā,at her wedding,; cf. .—
Esp., a lamp: ferreae lampades,: aënea,: praecinctae lampades auro,: accipere oleum cum lampadibus,.—
Trop.
From the Grecian torch-race (which consisted in keeping the torch burning during the race and handing it, still lighted, to the next one), are borrowed the expressions: lampada tradere alicui, to give or resign one's occupation to another: nunc cursu lampada tibi trado,now it is your turn,: quasi cursores, vitai lampada tradunt,i. e. they finish their course, die,: qui prior es, cur me in decursu lampada poscis?i. e. do you wish to succeed to my estate while I am yet alive?.—
In gen., splendor, brightness, lustre: aeterna mundl,; cf.: rosea sol alte lampade lucens,: Phoebeae lampadis instar,the light of the sun, the sun,: postera cum primā lustrabat lampade terras Orta dies,the first beams of light, first rays of dawn,.—
Hence, poet., like lumen, for day: octavoque fere candenti lumine solis Aut etiam nonā reddebant lampade vitam,on the ninth day,; so of the moonlight: decima lampas Phoebes,; cf.: cum se bina formavit lampade Phoebe,i. e. after two moons,: lampade Phoebes sub decima,the tenth month,.—
A meteor resembling a torch: emicant et faces, non nisi cum decidunt visae. Duo genera earum: lampades vocant plane faces, alterum bolidas,; cf. : nunc sparso lumine lampas emicuit caelo,; .

la:noun:lamentum.html:
lāmentum, i, n.
perh. for clamentum, from clamo
,
a wailing, moaning, weeping, lamentation, lament (class., only in plur.): virum, Lachm.: negat se velle mortem suam dolore amicorum et lamentis vacare,: se lamentis lacrimisque dedere,: lamentis lacrimisque extinctos prosequi,: lamenta ac lacrimas cito ponunt,: in sordibus, lamentis luctuque jacēre, Cis. Pis. 36, 88: lamentis gemituque et femineo ululatu Tecta fremunt,: per lamenta ... muliebriter ferre,.—Transf., of hens, .—Sing.: assume super Syrum lamentum,;

la:noun:lama.html:
lāma, ae, f. (cf.: lacus, lacer).
Aslough, bog, fen: lacuna id est aquae collectio, quam alii lamam, alii lustrum, Paul. ex Müll.: viribus uteris per clivos, flumina, lamas,.—
A kind of mastic: Pistacia lentiscus, Linn.; (al. lainam).

la:verb:lamentor.html:
lāmentor, ātus, 1,
v. dep. n. and a. [lamentum], to wail, moan, weep, lament (class.).
Neutr.: lamentari, cruciari,: quod nunc lamentari,: praeter ceteras lamentari,: lapides flere ac lamentari cogere,: Hebiliter lamentari,; : ac plangere,: quid ego hic animo lamentor, Enn. ap. Don. (Ann. v. 210 Vahl.): Thetis quoque lamentando pausam fecit filio,.—
Act., to weep over a person or thing, to bewail, lament, bemoan: conqueri fortunam advorsam, non lamentari decet, Id viri est officium; fletus muliebri ingenio additus est, Pac. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 268 Rib.): nam haec quidem vita mors est, quam lamentari possem,: caecitatem,: se ipsum,: suam matrem mortuam,: ut nemo ad lamentandam tanti imperii calamitatem relinquatur,.—With object.clause, ; so, cum lamentamur, non apparere labores Nostros,.—
Pass. (poet. and late Lat.; cf. lamento).—Part. perf. in pass. signif. (poet.), wept over, bewailed: fata per urbem Lamentata,; so, Dindyma,resounding with lamentations,.—
Impers. pass.: maeretur, fletur, lamentatur diebus plusculis,.

lāmĭna or lammĭna, and sync. lamna (e. g. ; ; ; ; also,
lamina,), ae, f., a thin piece of metal, wood, marble, etc., a plate, leaf, layer, lamina [root la, = ἐλα- of ἐλαύνω; cf. ἐλατός].
Lit. Laminae ardentes, red-hot plates, instruments of torture for slaves, ; so, candens,; without adj.: advorsum laminas, crucesque conpedisque,; .—

erat, ; cf. fulva,a gold piece, gold,: inimicus lamnae,foe to money,: tuas opes ... laminas utriusque materiae,of each precious metal,.—

A saw, .—

The tender shell of an unripe nut, .
